title: Savings Catalyst: Field Experiments & Rollout Steps for Batching / Cache / Quant
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Objective: run a tightly scoped set of real-customer field experiments that combine selective batching, prefix/KV cache policies, and model quantization to validate end-to-end unit-cost savings without regressions in latency or quality. This ticket coordinates the pilot plan, gating criteria, dashboards, and the first controlled rollouts into Dedicated and Hosted traffic lanes.

Scope:
- Identify three representative customer workloads (chat short-turn, assistant multi-turn, embedding-heavy search) with telemetry baselines.
- Create experiment matrix that crosses batching window (continuous vs fixed micro-batches), cache TTL/policy (per-route prefix TTLs, KV eviction heuristics), and quant settings (4-bit per-layer profiles).
- Instrument telemetry and quality checks (ROUGE/Response-fluency heuristics, latency p95, token unit cost).
- Run canary in dev -> staging -> limited-hosted -> dedicated pockets, capturing roll-forward/rollback playbook.

Deliverables:
1) Experiment registry doc (matrix + expected outcome per cell).
2) Telemetry dashboard with segmented unit-cost, latency, and quality deltas.
3) Rollout runbook with automated guard rails and rollback triggers.
4) Decision memo with recommended default profiles and opt-in signals for customers.

Success criteria (overall):
- Demonstrated >=9% token-cost reduction on at least two workload archetypes with no more than 2% measurable quality degradation and latency p95 within SLA (1.5x baseline).
- Clear signal-to-noise in dashboards enabling productization of at least one automatic savings knob by runtime-1.22.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment matrix defined and reviewed by Eng/Research/SEs
Dashboards show baseline and experiment segments with stable ingestion for 72+ hours
Runbook includes automated rollback thresholds and test scenarios
Decision memo approved by PM leadership and ENG owner assigned to productize the winning profile

metrics: Target token unit cost reduction: >=9% for at least two workload archetypes
Latency SLA: p95 no worse than 1.5x baseline during steady state
Quality guardrail: automated metric delta <2% (measured via profile-specific eval harness)
False-positive rollback rate <5% across all automated guardrails
risks: Quality regressions that are not captured by our automated heuristics (mitigation: manual eval slices + higher-fidelity evals)
Telemetry blind spots for edge-cases leading to noisy signals (mitigation: add targeted traces and user-id bucketing)
Interference between batching and cache policies causing tail latency spikes (mitigation: staged concurrency caps and chaos testing)
Customer dissatisfaction from unexpected model output differences (mitigation: customer-facing comms + opt-out path)
Operational complexity for Dedicated customers with strict isolation (mitigation: a dedicated safe-mode knob and pre-approved profile list)
